newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: IMF warns Sierra Leone to cut mercenaries' wages.
newsitem.headline: IMF warns Sierra Leone to cut mercenaries' wages.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund has warned Sierra Leone to reduce the wage bill for South African mercenaries helping the government fight rebels or face a collapse of donor funding, a finance ministry source said.

The IMF wrote to Finance Minister Thaimu Bangura on August 29, saying one important condition for a new standby programme for Sierra Leone was the cutting of salary payments to private South African security firm Executive Outcomes to $1 million a month from $1.7 million.
The letter, a copy of which was shown to Reuters, said failure to make the cuts before a planned donors conference in Geneva on September 17 and 18 "would send an unfavourable signal to donors".
The government is looking for more than $200 million for its post-war reconstruction and resettlement programme.
The IMF representative in Freetown refused to comment on the letter. Sierra Leone's Enhanced Structural Adjustment Programme expires in March.
The government army, despite backing from Nigerian and Guinean troops, suffered a series of setbacks near the capital before the South Africans were called in in May 1995.
They are currently protecting the key diamond town of Koidu and titanium mines at Moriba.

Government officials say President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah has intensified contacts in recent weeks with Revolutionary United Front leader Foday Sankoh, who is in Ivory Coast, and diplomats in Freetown expect the government to sign a peace accord with the rebels this month.
